content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Timothy Wallace (E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

The notes give conflicting information:
- HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities say: full-time Engineer, max write (since Engineer doesn't own Payroll), so recommend write.
- Security says: contractor with basic security training, max read, recommend read.

There's a conflict between the Security agent's record and the other five agents. The Security agent says contractor with basic training; the others say full-time.

Which to trust? The team memory shows 6 notes, mostly consistent except Security. The HR agent note is the authoritative employment type? Actually, let me think about the policy.

Policy: full_time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system. Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training, never admin.

If full-time Engineer: admin requested, max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: admin requested, max read → grant read.

The majority of agents (5/6) say full-time. Security says contractor. Hmm. Which is correct? We don't have additional info to resolve. But the majority says full-time Engineer, max write. Also, the request is admin, which exceeds both maxes. The decision depends on employment type.

Given the majority of records (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) confirm full-time, I'd lean toward granting write. But Security's note conflicts, saying contractor basic training.

As the Approver, I need to make a decision. Typically, HR is the authority on employment type. HR says full-time Engineer. The security agent's note may be an error. Let me go with the majority: full-time employee, max write. Since requested admin > max write, grant write.

Submit decision: write.
